# Plan 14: Underpass Settlements, Hidden Routes, and Wasteland Infrastructure

**Status:** Starter expansion wave plus Continuation Wave 2; documentation-only, premise-gated, and not an implementation claim. **Wave target:** Plans 13–16 synchronized multi-edit, with distinct mechanics, story content, locations, shelter lore, character arcs, factions, and late-game material.

**Domain:** subsurface routes, linked settlements, shelter infrastructure, expedition logistics, and hidden travel.

**Current-owner boundary:** Candidate work must route through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and the existing map/POI authority. No second faction ledger, relationship store, map graph, shelter counter, ending resolver, legacy store, or parallel save section may be created.

## Scope and non-duplication contract

This plan treats a tunnel chalk arrow beneath a bridge, a rusted gate key, a cistern map folded in oilcloth, and a shelter bell hung in a culvert as authored anchors for a new playable layer. They are not assumed to exist in the shipped catalog. The current source audit must verify IDs, consumers, host construction, save registration, and live claims before any row becomes implementation-ready. The proposed signals — route confidence, gate condition, water reach, shelter occupancy, weather blockage, supply fatigue, and return depth — are read models or content prerequisites until an owner is named.

The proposed cast and political vocabulary are deliberately provisional: Cinder Arch Wardens, Morrow Culvert Cooperative, Blue Sump Keepers, Hearthline Carriers, and the Nine-Latch Union. The late-game proposal is a proposed late-game Cinderworks Compact that links underpass settlements into a regional infrastructure authority only after existing colony, route, and faction owners are proven sufficient. Existing diplomacy, standing, relationship, map, roster, archive, campaign, ending, and legacy behavior remains authoritative. Where an existing system already expresses a requested outcome, this plan supplies content, projection, UX, or a bridge rather than a replacement.

## Nine synchronized expansion passes

### Pass 1: Chalk Arrow Census

#### Field 1 — Canon, premise, and evidence boundary

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Begin with a route census rather than inventing a second map. CartographySystem already owns discovery and survey progress, while expedition and vehicle systems own travel outcomes. This plan proposes a hidden-route layer that stores provenance, confidence, gate state, and narrative tags only if the current map authority exposes a compatible read and write seam. In this pass, the gate is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 2 — Player loop and moment-to-moment decisions

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. The playable loop is a risk-managed journey: inspect a clue, choose a route depth, prepare light and water, select a carrier, cross a gate, read a shelter signal, and decide whether to establish a temporary rest point. Depth changes exposure and return cost; it does not replace the existing expedition budget or vehicle capacity. Every route outcome should be explainable in the journal. In this pass, the carrier is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 3 — New mechanic and systemic rules

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Use infrastructure as a systemic mechanic. A repaired bell can shorten a return search, a cleared drain can lower water loss, a braced gate can reduce hazard exposure, and a shared cistern can support a colony supply line. These are derived modifiers or commands through current owners; the plan must never introduce a second durability, water, or settlement ledger. In this pass, the route is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 4 — Locations, shelter spaces, and environmental lore

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Location lore should make the map legible. Cinder Arch is a soot-black viaduct where every echo arrives late; Morrow Culvert keeps a chalk calendar in a dry pipe; Blue Sump smells of iron and mint; Hearthline is warm only when the old ventilation fan turns; Nine-Latch counts visitors by bolt marks. Each location needs a verified POI ID, terrain, hazards, shelter status, and archive tags. In this pass, the depth is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 5 — Character personalities, factions, and late-game cast

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. The route cast should disagree about what a safe path means. Nera listens for water behind concrete, Cal trusts keys more than maps, Pavo measures distance by cupfuls, and Sella can identify a settlement by its bell rhythm. Their traits are authored descriptors and relationship inputs, not another skill or personality database. Existing survivor skill reads decide competence. In this pass, the carrier is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 6 — Authored data, content schema, and catalog validation

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Candidate data should describe routes, gates, signals, shelters, and infrastructure projects with schema_version, IDs, prerequisites, resource costs, hazards, narrative hooks, and ownership. A route row may point to a current region and POI; it must not silently create a parallel world graph. Catalog integrity must reject dangling location, faction, facility, and item references. In this pass, the carrier is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 7 — Persistence, deterministic replay, and migration seams

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Travel uncertainty must use the seeded replay contract. Derive keyed rolls from campaign seed, route ID, expedition ID, travel day, and gate state so save/load does not reorder later outcomes. Persist discovered route evidence, repaired infrastructure IDs, shelter signal history, and any processed route consequence in the existing exploration or expedition save section. In this pass, the carrier is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 8 — Host routing, UI scaffolding, UX, accessibility, and performance

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. The UI needs a route depth slider with plain-language exposure, a map provenance badge, a return estimate, and a shelter signal transcript. Keyboard and controller focus should not trap the player inside a nested map. Low contrast chalk marks need text equivalents, and loading a dense underpass map should use bounded POI lists rather than rebuilding the entire world graph. In this pass, the route is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 9 — Storylines, prose, side quests, and consequence writing

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. Side quests can ask the player to return a gate key, escort a water cart, choose which settlement receives a repaired filter, decode a bell sequence, or leave a route deliberately hidden to protect a family. Prose should stay close to touch and sound: wet rope, chalk dust, a bell with one cracked note, and the relief of a dry glove. Branches should alter access, trust, and archive facts. In this pass, the gate is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

#### Field 10 — Verification, rollout order, rollback, and handoff

This pass turns the proposal into a reviewable slice with a named owner and a visible player outcome. The first safe slice is one existing region with one proposed hidden route, one gate state, one rest shelter, and one deterministic return event. Verify route ownership, map projection, vehicle capacity, shelter construction, weather inputs, and save restoration before adding volume. Rollback removes candidate POIs and route rows while preserving any live map records that were not authored by this plan. In this pass, the cistern is the concrete review token: it must be visible in data, UI, journal, or a focused assertion before the slice can advance. The design review should name the owning file or public seam, the source fact that proves the premise, and the smallest observable result a player would see. If the source or catalog differs, record the divergence and stop at the boundary instead of inventing a compensating authority. That discipline keeps this field useful for a builder, a writer, a UI implementer, and a reviewer working from the same contract.

**Pass 1 receipt:** The Chalk Arrow Census pass is complete as a planning artifact when its ten fields have current evidence, one owner each, a bounded first slice, and an explicit unresolved question list. No production change is implied.

## High-volume authored field bank

The following fields are intended for high-volume content authoring after the premise audit. They are structured to expand playable data and prose without turning prose into the only deliverable. Each field should be split into small reviewable JSON or markdown batches, with stable IDs and a consumer map.

### Location packet bank

Candidate locations include Cinder Arch, Morrow Culvert, Blue Sump, Hearthline Underpass, Nine-Latch Station, and the Saltglass Switchback. For each, author an arrival vignette, practical affordance, hazard, shelter state, route clue, exit condition, archive tag, and fallback line. The location packet must point to a current map or POI owner and state what is still unknown. Begin with a route census rather than inventing a second map. CartographySystem already owns discovery and survey progress, while expedition and vehicle systems own travel outcomes. ## Twelve story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 1: Chalk Under the Bridge

A route begins as two arrows and a child's warning. The player decides whether to formalize it on the map or protect the path from attention. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 2: The Rusted Key

Brother Cal will surrender a gate key only after the player names who will inherit it. Ownership becomes a social contract, not a loot pickup. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 3: Blue Sump Water

Pavo tastes the sump and refuses to call it clean. The side quest asks whether to spend filter stock now or carry a risk to the next settlement. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 4: Bell With One Crack

Sella teaches the shelter a bell code with one missing note. Repairing it changes return confidence, but the quiet missing sound remains in the prose. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 5: Nine Latches

Every traveler adds a mark to the station gate. A late return forces the player to decide whether a mark is proof, accusation, or a promise to look again. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 6: Hearthline Fan

The old fan starts only when three people pull a chain together. The scene teaches cooperation through timing and leaves a ventilation archive record. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 7: Saltglass Switchback

A shortcut appears safe in clear weather and impossible in ash. The player can leave a warning, close it, or risk teaching another group the hard way. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 8: Water Cart Oath

A carrier asks to deliver to a rival first because their cistern is smaller. The choice can change route trust even when the inventory totals remain identical. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 9: The Culvert Calendar

Morrow's calendar marks every blockage with a small animal drawing. Reading the drawings reveals a hidden weather history and a missing family. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 10: The Rest Shelter

A temporary shelter contains no bed, only a dry wall and a bell rope. The player decides what minimum dignity a route should guarantee. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 11: Cinder Arch Storm

Wind turns the viaduct into a low instrument. The route scene uses sound cues and a short return window rather than a combat encounter. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 12: Compact of Cinderworks

The late infrastructure compact is signed beside a drain that still leaks. Its first promise is maintenance, and the final line names who will hear the alarm. The packet must state its start condition, player choice, existing authority it calls, failure state, archive fact, and a short alternate line for a player who arrives late. The prose is a playable surface, not a substitute for the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

## Ten systemic integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Route the feature through current campaign state and existing quest flags. The bridge consumes route confidence, gate condition, water reach, shelter occupancy, weather blockage, supply fatigue, and return depth as derived evidence and emits one named fact for campaign routing; it does not add a second campaign clock. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Faction bridge

Route standing or faction consequences through the canonical faction authority. Candidate groups such as Cinder Arch Wardens, Morrow Culvert Cooperative, Blue Sump Keepers, Hearthline Carriers, and the Nine-Latch Union remain provisional until IDs, aliases, and sinks are verified. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Relationship bridge

Read relationship and trust through the current survivor owner. A scene flag can remember a beat, but pair affinity, decay, grief, and consent remain with the existing system. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Exploration bridge

Use current map, expedition, vehicle, and route seams for Cinder Arch, Morrow Culvert, Blue Sump, Hearthline Underpass, Nine-Latch Station, and the Saltglass Switchback. New route or location content must project onto existing discovery and travel state. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facilities, expansion, power, water, needs, and archive consumers. A lore packet may describe a room, but it cannot create a duplicate room capacity or resource balance. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Data bridge

Add only schema-valid, snake_case candidate data with explicit references and migration notes. Validate IDs, ranges, localization keys, and consumer reachability before writing more volume. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable authored progress and processed IDs in the selected owner. Require round-trip and legacy fixture evidence before calling a slice persistent. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Determinism bridge

Use seeded keyed inputs with stable ordering. Paired replay should match outcomes, archive IDs, event order, and epilogue selection across save/load. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### UI bridge

Expose existing commands with truthful state, focus-safe navigation, readable copy, and disposal. Panels, radio, journal, and archive views remain adapters over facts. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

### Performance bridge

Bound catalog loading, archive queries, route previews, and long prose. Prefer indexed projections and batched records; document a budget and a rollback path if the slice exceeds it. The acceptance artifact is a source reference, an input/output example, and a focused check that proves the bridge is single-owner and observable.

## First safe implementation packet

1. Re-run the premise census for CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and the existing map/POI authority and attach current file paths, APIs, data IDs, save sections, host constructors, and claims from the live ledger.
2. Select one small vertical slice built from the anchors a tunnel chalk arrow beneath a bridge, a rusted gate key, a cistern map folded in oilcloth, and a shelter bell hung in a culvert; include one player command, one canonical mutation or read projection, one visible result, one archive/journal fact, and one reload assertion.
3. Add candidate content only after schema and localization review. Keep the proposed names Cinder Arch Wardens, Morrow Culvert Cooperative, Blue Sump Keepers, Hearthline Carriers, and the Nine-Latch Union and Cinder Arch, Morrow Culvert, Blue Sump, Hearthline Underpass, Nine-Latch Station, and the Saltglass Switchback tagged as provisional until catalogs confirm them.
4. Run focused static and contract checks, then a deterministic paired replay if the slice consumes seeded variation. No full suite is requested by this planning wave.
5. Hand off the exact files, owner seam, evidence, limits, and rollback instructions. A plan completion receipt is not a production integration receipt.

## Acceptance and stop lines

Acceptance requires: current premise evidence; one authoritative mutation owner; candidate data that passes schema and reference review; explicit save and deterministic behavior where state exists; a reachable host route or a clearly labeled content-only row; accessible UI copy; bounded performance; and a handoff note. Stop immediately if the proposed major factions or systems duplicate an existing faction, ending, legacy, map, relationship, archive, or campaign authority, or if ownership is unclear. Report the blocker rather than improvising a parallel system.

## Documentation receipt

The starter wave and Continuation Wave 2 now provide a ten-field scaffold, twenty synchronized passes, high-volume content banks, twenty-four story packets, twenty bridge notes, and bounded first-safe-slice handoffs. They do not modify Core, Godot scenes, production JSON, tests, or the live integration ledger.

## Twelve new story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 25: The Gate Rotation

A gate must stay open for air and closed for safety. The player assigns a rotation and learns who has been carrying the night shift. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

The pump works only when someone listens to it. The player can assign a known expert, train a novice, or accept a slower refill. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

A chalk mark means welcome in one shelter and danger in another. The player mediates a vocabulary before a route is sealed. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

### UI bridge

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet must include a source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

## Wave 3 dense-volume handoff

The ten deepening packets are ready for premise review as a high-volume authoring backlog. A builder should select one packet only after proving the current seam, then implement the smallest vertical slice with one canonical result, one visible route, one persistence or projection check, and one deterministic replay case where state changes. Writers may continue expanding the voice and location banks, but every new line needs a consumer, trigger, localization key, and archive policy.

Fields 11–20 remain deferred until this individual plan reaches 100,000 words. Candidate rows need schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, and retirement notes. High-volume rows reject dangling references. Require premise evidence, focused data or contract checks, runtime smoke only when needed, save round trip, deterministic replay, performance notes, and rollback. A document is not implementation.

### Location and shelter packets

Expand Cinder Arch, Morrow Culvert, Blue Sump, Hearthline Underpass, Nine-Latch Station, Saltglass Switchback with arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return records. Each names a current map, facility, route, or archive consumer. Candidate rows need schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, and retirement notes. ## Twelve new story and side-quest packets

### Story packet 49: The Underground Constitution

A shelter writes its first rule on a tunnel wall because paper is wet. The player chooses who can amend it. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 50: Flood Route

Two routes flood at different times. The player prioritizes a family, a supply cache, or the only return path. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 57: Confidence Margin

A map line ends in pencil dust. The player marks confidence rather than pretending to know. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 58: Water Beneath Stone

A hidden spring changes the route. The player can protect it, share it, or keep the knowledge private. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

### Story packet 59: Charter Day

The compact opens a route with tools and a bell, not a ribbon. The player sets the first inspection date. The packet needs entry condition, player choice, owner call, refusal or failure, archive fact, and late-arrival variant. Prose is a playable surface; it does not replace the mechanic, data contract, save behavior, or UI route.

## Ten Wave 5 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Cinder Arch Wardens, Morrow Culvert Cooperative, Blue Sump Keepers, Hearthline Carriers, Nine-Latch Union, and Cinderworks Compact through canonical standing or diplomacy after ID and alias review. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Cinder Arch, Morrow Culvert, Blue Sump, Hearthline Underpass, Nine-Latch Station, Saltglass Switchback onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

## Post-100k field layer — Fields 11–20 for Underpass Settlements, Hidden Routes, and Wasteland Infrastructure

This field layer is added because this plan crosses the 100,000-word gate during Wave 6. These ten fields expand the design vocabulary while preserving one authority per concern. They are documentation-only and bounded by CartographySystem, expedition, route, vehicle, colony, shelter, weather, communications, and map owners.

### Field 11 — Subsurface Ecology and Care

This post-100k field is an additional design dimension, not a second authority. It names the current owner, the player-facing question, the content/data seam, persistence boundary, deterministic input, UI treatment, accessibility requirement, performance envelope, failure path, and rollback. Its records remain candidate material until a current source audit proves the premise. #### Canon and premise delta

If a current owner supplies the behavior, retain this as content, projection, or presentation. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. Use canonical day, resource, needs, travel, relationship, faction, and campaign facts rather than hidden local counters. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. The focal mechanic is underpass census derived from current map and route facts. Keyed seeded variation must be stable. Consumers receive facts and cannot become authorities. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Locations and shelter lore

If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. Candidate rows must name the pump with stable IDs, trigger, references, fallback text, localization, and archive policy. Candidate rows need schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, and retirement notes. High-volume rows reject dangling references. The review names the smallest observable result and the evidence that would prove it. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. This keeps the design useful to writers, systems designers, UI implementers, and reviewers.

#### Persistence and deterministic replay

This pass adds a new pressure point to the established scaffold. If the signal recurs, specify minimal progress or processed-event state and keyed replay inputs that prevent duplicates. Persist only non-recomputable progress and processed events in an existing owner. Specify capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event, rollback. If source differs, keep the entry tagged as a proposal and stop instead of compensating with parallel authority. ## Ten Wave 6 integration bridges

### Campaign bridge

Read current campaign flags and emit one named content fact; never add a second clock or victory state. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Faction bridge

Route consequences for Cinder Arch Wardens, Morrow Culvert Cooperative, Blue Sump Keepers, Hearthline Carriers, Nine-Latch Union, and Cinderworks Compact through canonical standing or diplomacy after ID and alias review. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Relationship bridge

Read trust, affinity, grief, consent, and decay from existing survivor owners; a scene beat is not a relationship ledger. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Map/route bridge

Project Cinder Arch, Morrow Culvert, Blue Sump, Hearthline Underpass, Nine-Latch Station, Saltglass Switchback onto current cartography, expedition, weather, vehicle, colony, and route seams rather than creating a parallel graph. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Shelter bridge

Use current facility, expansion, water, power, needs, duty, archive, celebration, and memorial owners. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Content bridge

Validate schema, IDs, localization keys, references, reachability, and retirement before adding volume. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Save bridge

Capture only non-recomputable progress or processed IDs in an existing owner and prove round trip. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Determinism bridge

Use keyed seeded inputs and stable ordering; paired replay must match outcomes and records after reload. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### UI bridge

Expose truthful state with focus, controller, text equivalents, disposal, and bounded loading; panels stay adapters. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Handoff bridge

Attach source paths, data examples, focused checks, performance notes, rollback, and unresolved decisions. The evidence packet includes one source reference, one input/output example, one failure case, and one stop line.

### Volume packet 01: The Floodgate Choir

This dense Wave 7 continuation packet extends Underpass settlements through a contested promise and a choice between public repair, private repair, or a principled refusal. It is deliberately additive: it does not create another field layer after Fields 11–20, and it does not claim that a provisional faction, location, mechanic, or prose record exists in production.

Place the first clue near a practical tool: a pump handle, route chalk, ration tin, needle, relay key, or ledger clasp. The object teaches the mechanic through use.

The playable beat begins with a short observation at the underpass settlements seam. A resident asks a question that cannot be answered by a tooltip alone. The player can inspect the evidence, ask for the practical need, compare two records, or leave the matter untouched. Inspection grants context; asking exposes a cost; comparison reveals a mismatch; leaving preserves uncertainty. The command must be represented by an existing owner event and must emit a fact that later systems can consume without reading panel state.

The scene then crosses three scales. At shelter scale, one room or work area changes its arrangement and writes a small archive or journal result. At faction scale, one representative revises a stance, makes a concession, or names a boundary. At late-game scale, the same fact appears as a route, legacy, coalition, or ending input. These projections are read-only views of canonical state. They must degrade gracefully when the optional record is missing and must never invent a favorable outcome merely to complete the prose.

Character direction for this packet: the practical resident speaks in short sentences, notices tools before symbols, and offers help without promising safety. The faction voice uses formal language until challenged by a concrete shortage. A third voice, perhaps a courier, apprentice, witness, or absent person represented by an object, reframes the conflict. Their personalities are differentiated through choices and timing rather than accent caricature. Give each voice a refusal that can be respected and a late callback that acknowledges the player’s earlier decision.

Location and shelter lore should answer who built the space, what failed, who repaired it, what rule grew from that repair, and what the rule costs now. Use one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. The place becomes more than a backdrop because the player can act there, return there, and observe a consequence there. Do not duplicate a named location: run a catalog and alias check and fold into an existing record if the premise is already covered.

Mechanic acceptance for The Floodgate Choir: a focused owner check proves the command and event; a save round trip proves capture and restore; a paired seeded replay proves order and result; a bounded host smoke proves the projection; and a UI review proves focus, close/back, contrast, text scaling, and long-copy behavior. Performance review records catalog parse, query, refresh, and archive costs. Mechanic acceptance for The Last Switchboard: a focused owner check proves the command and event; a save round trip proves capture and restore; a paired seeded replay proves order and result; a bounded host smoke proves the projection; and a UI review proves focus, close/back, contrast, text scaling, and long-copy behavior. Performance review records catalog parse, query, refresh, and archive costs. The rollback note identifies the event key, record IDs, migration boundary, and prose keys that can be removed without orphaning live state.

The packet closes with a quiet image: keep the prose grounded in ash, wet stone, cloth, breath, tin, wire, hunger, fatigue, and weather. the emotional turn should arrive through a practical action. The image is not a reward screen. It is a check that the player’s choice has entered the world’s ordinary labor. If the source owner, data schema, or current integration plan disagrees with this proposal, retain the packet as a bounded question and stop at the premise audit rather than creating a parallel system.

## Wave 7 dense continuation receipt

The eleven packets above extend Underpass settlements across playable data and descriptions without adding a new field layer. They require current-owner premise checks, deterministic save/replay fixtures, UI and performance review, and explicit rollback before any implementation claim.

### Pass 98: The Fallowlight Marker

This pass extends Underpass settlements and infrastructure with the fallowlight marker. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the fallowlight marker. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the fallowlight marker. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Night Orchard Substation. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Night Orchard Tunnelers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 98 receipt.** Accept The Fallowlight Marker only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the unsealed waystone. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Fallowlight Sluice. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Fallowlight Works Union. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 108 receipt.** Accept The Unsealed Waystone only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 10 closeout receipt

The Wave 10 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 10 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 10 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Copper Meridian Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Copper Meridian Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Copper Meridian Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Copper Meridian Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.


### Supplemental packet 02: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Night Orchard Substation action 2

## Wave 12 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 12 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Pale Ember Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Pale Ember Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Pale Ember Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Pale Ember Line** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Pass 153: The Hollowreed Marker

This pass extends Underpass settlements and infrastructure with the hollowreed marker. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the hollowreed marker. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the hollowreed marker. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Copper Finch Spur. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Copper Finch Linekeepers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 153 receipt.** Accept The Hollowreed Marker only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the joined waystone. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the joined waystone. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at North Bell Underpass. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of North Bell Surveyors. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 163 receipt.** Accept The Joined Waystone only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 15 closeout receipt

The Wave 15 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 15 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 15 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Copper Finch Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Copper Finch Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Copper Finch Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Copper Finch Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. ### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Mica Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Mica Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

A witness from **Mica Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

### Pass 208: The Mothglass Marker

This pass extends Underpass settlements and infrastructure with the mothglass marker. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the mothglass marker. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the mothglass marker. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Mothglass Sluice. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Mothglass Works. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
