It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the rebound waystone. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the rebound waystone. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Ivory Ash Pumpway. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Ivory Ash Tunnelers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 218 receipt.** Accept The Rebound Waystone only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 20 closeout receipt

The Wave 20 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 20 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 20 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Penny Reed Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Penny Reed Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Penny Reed Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Penny Reed Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. ### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Amber Finch Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Amber Finch Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Amber Finch Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Amber Finch Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Pass 263: The Cinderlace Marker

This pass extends Underpass settlements and infrastructure with the cinderlace marker. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the cinderlace marker. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the cinderlace marker. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at West Chime Underpass. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of West Chime Surveyors. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 263 receipt.** Accept The Cinderlace Marker only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the recast waystone. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the recast waystone. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Hollow Reed Spur. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Hollow Reed Linekeepers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 273 receipt.** Accept The Recast Waystone only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 25 closeout receipt

The Wave 25 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 25 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 25 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Hollow Reed Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Hollow Reed Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Hollow Reed Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Hollow Reed Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. ### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Clear Finch Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Clear Finch Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Clear Finch Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Clear Finch Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Pass 318: The Frostpetal Marker

This pass extends Underpass settlements and infrastructure with the frostpetal marker. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the frostpetal marker. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the frostpetal marker. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Darkwater Pumpway. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Darkwater Tunnelers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 318 receipt.** Accept The Frostpetal Marker only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

### Pass 328: The Recast Waystone

This pass extends Underpass settlements and infrastructure with the recast waystone. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the recast waystone. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the recast waystone. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Frostpetal Sluice. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Frostpetal Works. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 328 receipt.** Accept The Recast Waystone only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 30 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 30 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Amber Roost Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Amber Roost Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Amber Roost Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Green Votive Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Green Votive Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Green Votive Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Green Votive Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Starling Ash Works** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Pass 373: The Red Willow Marker

This pass extends Underpass settlements and infrastructure with the red willow marker. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the red willow marker. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through CartographySystem, expedition and route owners, vehicle and colony owners, ShelterExpansionSystem, WeatherSystem, CommunicationsSystem, and map/POI consumers. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the red willow marker. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Cobalt Finch Spur. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Cobalt Finch Linekeepers. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

Pin a seeded event key, input order, and expected result. A paired replay must produce the same standing, route, roster, archive, or ending projection. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, and hidden random choices in authored content.

## Wave 35 supplemental depth packets

### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Cobalt Finch Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Cobalt Finch Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. ## Wave 35 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 35 extended depth packet 01: brokered truce calendar at Red Willow Sluice

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The brokered truce calendar begins as a premise audit around Red Willow Sluice. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Red Willow Sluice, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for Underpass settlements and infrastructure. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Cobalt Finch Spur, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Cobalt Finch Spur notices labor and weather. A representative of Red Willow Works speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Cobalt Finch Linekeepers remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Red Willow Works, Cobalt Finch Linekeepers, Ashriver Tunnelers, and South Harrow Surveyors by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Red Willow Works wants a reliable public record, Cobalt Finch Linekeepers protects a route custom, Ashriver Tunnelers values a scarce repair skill, and South Harrow Surveyors demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for brokered truce calendar carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Ashriver Pumpway, South Harrow Underpass, Ashriver Tunnelers, and South Harrow Surveyors provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

## Wave 36 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 36 extended depth packet 01: witnessed resource compact at Amber Cinder Sluice

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The witnessed resource compact begins as a premise audit around Amber Cinder Sluice. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Amber Cinder Sluice, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for Underpass settlements and infrastructure. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Mossglass Spur, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Mossglass Spur notices labor and weather. A representative of Amber Cinder Works speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

A witness linked to Mossglass Linekeepers remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Amber Cinder Works, Mossglass Linekeepers, Silver Rain Tunnelers, and East Yarrow Surveyors by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Amber Cinder Works wants a reliable public record, Mossglass Linekeepers protects a route custom, Silver Rain Tunnelers values a scarce repair skill, and East Yarrow Surveyors demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for archive lantern covenant carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Silver Rain Pumpway, East Yarrow Underpass, Silver Rain Tunnelers, and East Yarrow Surveyors provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

## Wave 36 extended depth receipt

The extended layer is documentation-only. Promotion requires current premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable content, deterministic persistence and replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence.

## Continuation Wave 37 — Passes 395–405

This synchronized continuation keeps Fields 11–20 active. It adds new provisional factions, late-game organizations, locations, shelter customs, survivor voices, mechanics, side quests, UI/UX scaffolds, and performance or replay gates without claiming production implementation or creating parallel mutable state.

## Wave 37 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 37 extended depth packet 01: public witness compact at Marrowlight Sluice

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The public witness compact begins as a premise audit around Marrowlight Sluice. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Marrowlight Sluice, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for Underpass settlements and infrastructure. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Blue Orchard Spur, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Blue Orchard Spur notices labor and weather. A representative of Marrowlight Works speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Blue Orchard Linekeepers remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Marrowlight Works, Blue Orchard Linekeepers, Copper Haze Tunnelers, and East Sable Surveyors by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Marrowlight Works wants a reliable public record, Blue Orchard Linekeepers protects a route custom, Copper Haze Tunnelers values a scarce repair skill, and East Sable Surveyors demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for public witness compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Copper Haze Pumpway, East Sable Underpass, Copper Haze Tunnelers, and East Sable Surveyors provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

## Wave 38 closeout receipt

The Wave 38 material remains documentation-only. Promotion requires current-source premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, reachable data, deterministic save and replay fixtures, UI/accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary.

## Wave 38 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 38 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: Underpass settlements and infrastructure — Red Vale Spur action 1

The scene opens at **Red Vale Spur**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Red Vale Spur, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **Red Vale Linekeepers** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Wave 38 extended depth packet 01: shared burden compact at Hearthblue Sluice

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The shared burden compact begins as a premise audit around Hearthblue Sluice. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Hearthblue Sluice, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for Underpass settlements and infrastructure. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Red Vale Spur, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Red Vale Spur notices labor and weather. A representative of Hearthblue Works speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to Red Vale Linekeepers remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Hearthblue Works, Red Vale Linekeepers, Lumen Fog Tunnelers, and West Bracken Surveyors by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Hearthblue Works wants a reliable public record, Red Vale Linekeepers protects a route custom, Lumen Fog Tunnelers values a scarce repair skill, and West Bracken Surveyors demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for shared burden compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Lumen Fog Pumpway, West Bracken Underpass, Lumen Fog Tunnelers, and West Bracken Surveyors provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.
